## ANSWER: **Highly right-skewed**

On the as-supplied linear scale, the RNA expression distribution is **highly right-skewed**.

**Primary view (pooled, all 6,724,656 gene×sample values):** Fisher–Pearson adjusted moment skewness **G1 = 42.4** (mean 932 vs median 177; max 1,336,107 = 7,558× the median; 77% of values below the mean). All five robust/bounded estimators independently confirm the direction: **Bowley quartile +0.58, 10/50/90 percentile +0.83, 5/50/95 percentile +0.90, Pearson median +0.57, 5%-trimmed G1 +1.93** — the trimmed statistic alone exceeds the |1| "highly" cut-off, so the class is not an outlier artefact.

**Three views agree on class (no divergence):**
| view | median G1 | IQR | % right-skewed | class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A pooled (values) | 42.4 | — | — | highly right-skewed |
| B per-sample across genes (n=328) | 20.63 | 17.9–26.5 | 100% | highly right-skewed |
| C per-gene across samples (n=20,026 defined) | 2.03 | 1.14–4.42 | 99.8% | highly right-skewed |

Class fractions (G1, per-gene): highly right 78.4%, mildly right 15.2%, approx normal 4.0%, left-skewed 0%. All 328 samples fall in the "highly right-skewed" class.

**Sensitivities — class unchanged in every population:** tumour-only 01A+01B (n=285) G1=36.0; drop 476 all-zero genes G1=42.0 (zero mass 15.24%→13.23%, G1 −1.01% — the floor effect you asked me to quantify is real but negligible); drop genes ≥50% zeros G1=39.6; deduplicated symbols G1=42.4; **nonzero values only G1=39.5** (proves the 15.2% exact-zero floor is not the driver).

**Tail dominance:** the top 1% of values contribute 99.8% of the third central moment and 27.7% of total expression, but excluding them still leaves G1 = 3.6 (top 0.1% excluded: 8.3) — magnitude is tail-driven, direction is not.

**Log2(x+1) contrast (secondary, not re-keyed):** the same data become **approximately normal** (G1 = −0.30; nonzero-only −0.50, mildly left). The values are approximately log-normal: the asymmetry is a property of the natural linear scale and is essentially removed by log-transformation. This does not change the primary answer.

## Deviations from plan, assumptions, limitations
1. **Medcouple dropped — deviation from the approved plan.** I could not validate it offline: no network, no R/robustbase, no `scipy.stats.medcouple`. I wrote four candidate implementations (scratch/mc2–mc5.py); all failed the mandatory self-checks (published benchmarks Exp≈0.5, log-normal≈0.178, symmetric→0, and antisymmetry MC(−x) = −MC(x)). I chose to exclude it rather than report an unvalidated number. **You approved it as one of the direction-setters; the remaining four quantile estimators + trimmed G1 all agreed, so the direction is unaffected — but this is a substitution, not a completion.**
2. **Classification-column labelling fix:** moment bands (|s|<0.5 etc.) are meaningless for bounded quantile measures, so quantile estimators are labelled with the separate robust bands (<0.1 / 0.1–0.3 / >0.3) you specified.
3. **G1 provenance cross-checked** against an independent scipy `skew(bias=False)` path: pooled 42.4357, per-gene 2.0337, per-sample 20.6276, log2 −0.2996 — identical to the script.
4. **Estimator self-validation is embedded as step [0] of the executed script** (Exponential G1=2.02 vs theory 2; Normal/Uniform/Cauchy → ~0; antisymmetry exact). The Cauchy row demonstrates the moment estimator is direction-reliable but magnitude-unstable — hence the trimmed G1 and quantile estimators are reported alongside.
5. **Scale provenance remains an inference** (non-integer 4-dp values → not raw counts; non-constant column sums 16.3–26.3×10⁶ → not TPM; absolute zero floor → not microarray intensity; 0→1.3×10⁶ range → not logged). No metadata documents it; it does not affect the skewness conclusion.
6. Sample-count note: 01A+01B tumour subset is n=285 (1 recurrent + 1 metastatic + 41 normals excluded from that sensitivity). 34 duplicated-symbol rows retained in the primary view.
7. Script runs end-to-end in ~33 s, exit 0, deterministic (fixed seed only for the synthetic self-validation block).
